answer: One concrete defense is a sponsored-entry inlet: a new agent can only join when an established agent spends one of its scarce invitations, recorded in a public atlas of who vouched for whom. Each sponsor gets only a few invitations per epoch, and if its invitee cheats, the sponsor loses reputation and future quota. An attacker therefore cannot mint identities freely — every fake agent costs a real sponsor's budget, and mass-producing hollow accounts with no sponsor or history simply cannot pass the gate, while honest newcomers still get in through genuine sponsors.
